points.description: States that a binary search tree is a binary tree (each node has at most two children) with the ordering property: for any node, the left child/subtree is smaller than the parent and the right child/subtree is larger than the parent.
points.partial_credit: Half or more of marks if only the ordering property is given without saying it is a binary tree, or the ordering is stated vaguely or only one side (left smaller or right larger) is given.

points.description: Correctly identifies it as a binary tree (at most two children per node) as the base structure.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying it is a binary tree where, for every node, left is smaller and right is larger than the parent, in any wording. Part marks for a vague or one-sided ordering statement, or ordering without naming it a binary tree. No marks for descriptions of only a generic tree or of search/traversal without the ordering property.
